$$

$$

Suppose that $V=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$ Given that $B$ is an orthogonal basis for $V,$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
We find an orthogonal basis $B$ of $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1.** We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2.** We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{8}{8}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3.** We find the vector ${v}_{3}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-\frac{6}{8}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{18}{9}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-\frac{3}{4}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(4[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2} \\ 6 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=-\frac{3}{2},$ $c=\frac{3}{2},$ and $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{(-\frac{3}{2})}{(\frac{3}{2})}=-1.$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}| \\ \frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}| \\ \frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A,$ and an **orthonormal** basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that ${a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $|\,d\,|?$
after.worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{16}{16}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${v}_{3}$ dividing it by $‖{v}_{3}‖=\sqrt{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{3} & =\frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $|\,d\,|=|-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}|=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.$

$$

content.worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{16}{16}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${v}_{3}$ dividing it by $‖{v}_{3}‖=\sqrt{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{3} & =\frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $|\,d\,|=|-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}|=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.$

after.worked_solution:
We find an orthogonal basis $B$ of $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1.** We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2.** We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{6}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3.** We find the vector ${v}_{3}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-\frac{3}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{4}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=-1,$ $c=2,$ and $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{(-1)}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}.$

content.knowledge_point: Finding an Orthogonal Basis For the Column Space of a Matrix Given Some Orthogonal Columns
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 \\ -1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that ${a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
content.worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ 

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-(0)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ -3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{b}{c}=\frac{(-2)}{(2)}=-1.
$$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 10 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}| \\ \frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}| \\ \frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A,$ and an **orthonormal** basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that ${a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $|\,c\,|?$
after.worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 10 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-\frac{10}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{25}{5}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 10 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${v}_{3}$ dividing it by $‖{v}_{3}‖=\sqrt{10}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{3} & =\frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10} \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{10} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5} \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $|\,c\,|=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}.$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 10 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}| \\ \frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}| \\ \frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A,$ and an **orthonormal** basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that ${a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $|\,c\,|?$
content.worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 10 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-\frac{10}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{25}{5}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 10 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${v}_{3}$ dividing it by $‖{v}_{3}‖=\sqrt{10}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{3} & =\frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10} \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{10} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5} \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $|\,c\,|=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}.$
